# The Postbox Game

> A free mobile game for iPhone and Android that turns walks into a treasure hunt: players find real postboxes across the United Kingdom, name the royal cypher on each one to claim it once a day, and score more points for rarer cyphers on daily, weekly, monthly and all-time leaderboards.

The Postbox Game is free, with no ads. It covers postboxes in the United Kingdom only. Postbox data comes from OpenStreetMap (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL), and more than 90,000 UK postboxes are mapped.

## How it works

- Open the app on a walk. It counts the postboxes nearby, and a fuzzy compass shows roughly which way they lie, never their exact location.
- Stand within about 30 metres of a postbox and name the royal cypher on its front to claim it.
- Each postbox can be claimed once a day. A claim every day keeps a streak going.
- Players add friends with an invite link and compare scores on a friends-only leaderboard.
- Route mode shows how many postboxes, and how many points, lie on the way to a chosen destination.
- On Android, a standalone Wear OS app scans, shows the compass and claims from the watch.
- Players can report a missing postbox or a wrong cypher from the app. Accepted reports update everyone's scores and are passed back to OpenStreetMap.

## Points per royal cypher

The cypher shows which monarch reigned when the postbox was installed. Rarer cyphers score more.

- EVIIIR (Edward VIII, 1936): 12 points
- CIIIR (Charles III, 2022 onwards): 9 points
- EVIIR (Edward VII, 1901–1910): 9 points
- VR (Victoria, 1837–1901): 7 points
- GVR (George V, 1910–1936): 4 points
- GVIR (George VI, 1936–1952): 4 points
- GR (George, generic): 4 points
- SCOTTISH_CROWN (Scottish Crown, Scotland only): 4 points
- EIIR (Elizabeth II, 1952–2022): 2 points
